# ROSIE KETCH [italic]The Queen of the Outer Veil. Six records, four guitars, one voice you can hear over an atmosphere processor at full draw.[/italic]
## HOWDY, {colony} Pull up a crate. I was born on a terraforming hauler between two worlds that did not have names yet, and I learned to sing in a pressurised cargo bay because it had the best echo on the ship. My mother was a pipefitter. My daddy drove a crawler. Neither of them could carry a tune, but they could carry anything else, and that is what my songs are about.
If you are reading this on a colony terminal, you probably know the smell of processor exhaust, the sound of a dropship you were not expecting and the feeling of a mail run that came in without a letter for you. I wrote a song about each of those. You are why I keep going out past the Veil when the studio on Mars keeps asking me to stay.
[italic]Love, Rosie[/italic]
## WHAT IS NEW - [bold]Processor Lullaby[/bold], the sixth record, is out on cassette and on the relay. Recorded live in the machine hall at Oxley's Butte, with the dam running underneath. - [bold]The Dust Road Tour[/bold] reaches twelve colonies this year. Rosie plays wherever there is a floor and a power socket. - [bold]The Golden Relay.[/bold] Rosie was nominated for Best Frontier Record for the fourth time. She did not attend. She was playing a canteen on Chance's Claim that night and says it was the better crowd.
## THE DUST DEVILS - [bold]Amos Tull[/bold], banjo. A former Colonial Marshal. He does not talk about it, and the banjo does it for him. - [bold]Marisol Pike[/bold], fiddle and harmony. Learned on a fiddle carved out of a cargo pallet. Still plays it. - [bold]Big Dee Okonjo[/bold], upright bass. Tall enough to change a ceiling panel without a ladder, which is how he got the job. - [bold]Clem[/bold], drums. Clem is a Working Joe. Clem keeps perfect time. Clem has asked us to state that Clem does not have a favourite song.
